will_worship LORD [future; all the ends of the earth will turn to him] The nations are said to be ruled by the LORD, whose kingdom it is. All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to him, and all the relatives of the nations will worship before him, including the rich and those who go down to the dust.

The speaker, identified in the heading as a psalm by David, declares that the LORD is his shepherd and that he will lack nothing. He says he will fear no evil even when walking through the valley of the shadow of death because the LORD is with him. He expresses confidence that goodness and loving kindness will follow him all his days and that he will dwell in the LORD's house forever.

l: house of the LORD (the LORD's house), Psalms
s: belongs_to the LORD The LORD's house is the destination people invite the speaker to visit, which makes him glad. At the end of the unit it is named as the reason the speaker will seek Jerusalem's good.
The earth is declared the LORD's, together with its fullness and its inhabitants; it was founded by him upon the seas and established on the floods.

is_a holy place The LORD's hill is asked about in the question of who may ascend to it and stand in his holy place. It is described as a place that only a person of clean hands and a pure heart may approach.

l: person who may ascend (the one with clean hands and a pure heart), Psalms
s: A person qualified to ascend the LORD's hill by clean hands and a pure heart, free of falsehood and deceitful oaths. He receives the LORD's blessing and righteousness from the God of his salvation, belonging to Jacob's generation seeking God's face.

is_a everlasting doors [addressed to lift up their heads] The gates, also called the everlasting doors, are commanded twice to lift up their heads and be lifted up. This is so that the King of glory, the LORD, may come in.
David asks that his enemies not triumph over him. He says they are many and hate him with cruel hatred, and he asks the LORD to consider them and to deliver him.

l: those who fear the LORD, Psalms
s: People who fear the LORD are taught by him which way to choose, then enjoy a soul at ease, offspring inheriting the land, his friendship, and revelation of his covenant.

includes sins of his youth [David asks the LORD not to remember them] David asks the LORD not to remember the sins of his youth or his transgressions, but to remember him according to loving kindness. He asks the LORD to pardon his iniquity, which he calls great, and to forgive all his sins.

l: assembly of evildoers (those David hates), Psalms
s: David says he hates the assembly of evildoers and will not sit with the wicked. They are described alongside deceitful men, hypocrites, sinners, and bloodthirsty men whose hands are full of wickedness and whose right hands are full of bribes. David asks not to be gathered with them.

David claims to have walked in his integrity and offers it as the basis for asking the LORD to judge him. He resolves to keep walking in it, and in the same verse asks for redemption and mercy. He states that his foot stands in an even place.

opposes David [they stumbled and fell] Evildoers, adversaries, and foes came at the speaker to eat up his flesh but stumbled and fell. An army and war may still rise against him, and false witnesses who breathe out cruelty have risen up against him. The speaker asks not to be delivered over to their desire and expects his head to be lifted up above them.

is_a tabernacle/tent of the LORD [place of refuge and inquiry] The LORD's house, also called his temple, pavilion, tabernacle, and tent, is the place the speaker most wants to dwell in all the days of his life. There he hopes to see the LORD's beauty and inquire, and the secret place of the tabernacle is where the LORD will hide him in trouble. It is also where he will offer sacrifices of joy and sing praises.

l: trust and confidence in God despite danger, Psalms
s: is_a attitude of David [stated in the face of army and war] The speaker states that his heart will not fear and that he will be confident even if an army encamps or war rises against him. He bases this on the LORD being his light, salvation, and strength, and on the LORD's protection in the day of trouble. He closes by affirming he is still confident of seeing the LORD's goodness and by urging himself to wait for the LORD, be strong, and take courage.

The wicked are workers of iniquity who speak peace to neighbors while harboring mischief. David asks they be repaid per their deeds; because they disregard the LORD's works, he will break them down and not build them up.

is_shepherded_by LORD [as requested in prayer] The LORD's people are described as having the LORD as their strength, and he is a stronghold of salvation to his anointed. David asks the LORD to save them, bless his inheritance, be their shepherd, and bear them up forever.

was_heard_by LORD David's petitions are a cry to the LORD for a response, made with hands lifted toward the Most Holy Place. They ask that he not be drawn away with the wicked, that the wicked be repaid, and later that the LORD's people be saved. David blesses the LORD because he has heard the voice of these petitions.

is_commanded_to_ascribe_to_the_lord glory and strength [command] The sons of the mighty are addressed in the opening verses and commanded to ascribe glory and strength to the LORD. They are also told to ascribe to him the glory due his name and to worship him in holy array.
The LORD's voice is powerful and majestic, sounding over the waters. It shatters Lebanon's cedars, shakes Kadesh's wilderness, flashes lightning, then brings deer to calve and strips forests bare.

is_due_to the LORD [due to his name] Glory is to be ascribed to the LORD, including the glory due his name, and he is described as the God of glory who thunders. In his temple, everything says, "Glory!"

l: anger and favor of the LORD, Psalms
s: A topic contrasting the LORD's brief anger with his lifelong favor: weeping lasts a night but joy comes in the morning; the speaker knew favor as mountain-strength and God's hidden face as trouble.
The LORD transforms David's mourning into dancing, removing sackcloth and clothing him with gladness, so his heart sings praise without silence and he vows to give thanks forever.

David's adversaries are proud, lying enemies who secretly lay a net, slander and persecute him, spread terror, and plot to kill him, making neighbors flee; David prays they be disappointed, silenced in Sheol, and their contemptuous lips mute.

l: saints and faithful (those who fear and trust the LORD), Psalms
s: The saints and faithful are those who fear the LORD, take refuge in him, and hope in him. Great goodness is stored up for them, and he hides them from human plotting and strife. They are urged to love him, be strong, and take courage.

David's affliction and grief: his eye, soul and body waste away, his life spent in sorrow and sighing. Strength fails through iniquity, bones waste, and he becomes a horror to acquaintances, forgotten like the dead and broken pottery, yet the LORD has seen and known.

David is a speaker who, after silence over his sin left him physically drained under the LORD's heavy hand, confessed and was forgiven. He then calls the LORD his hiding place, expects preservation and songs of deliverance, and urges the righteous to rejoice.
Everyone who is godly is urged to pray to the LORD in a time when he may be found. The psalm says that when the great waters overflow, they will not reach such a person.
experiences many sorrows The wicked are said to experience many sorrows. This contrasts with the one who trusts in the LORD, who is surrounded by loving kindness.
David's sin, silently kept, wasted his bones and sapped his strength; he then confessed without hiding his iniquity, and the LORD forgave it, leaving it covered.

results_in blessedness [for the one whose disobedience is forgiven] Forgiveness is presented as the source of blessing: the person whose disobedience is forgiven and whose sin is covered is blessed. David experienced it when he confessed his transgressions and the LORD forgave the iniquity of his sin.

l: those who fear him (those who fear the LORD), Psalms
s: Those who fear the LORD are a group for whom praise is fitting and who are called saints. They wait for him, trust his holy name, and hope in him. His angel encamps around and delivers them, and they lack nothing, unlike hungry young lions; seekers lack no good thing.

is_directed_to the LORD [with lyre and harp of ten strings] The psalm commands thanks to the LORD with the lyre and praise with the ten-stringed harp. It calls for a new song played skillfully with a shout of joy, and ends with the people's hearts rejoicing in him.

The LORD's word is right and powerful: by it and his breath the heavens and their army were made, the sea's waters gathered and the deeps stored. Since he spoke and it was done, all the earth should fear him.

Deliverance and trust: safety comes from the LORD, not from armies, kings' strength, or horses. He delivers those who fear him and hope in his loving kindness from death and keeps them alive in famine. The people respond by waiting, trusting his holy name, and praying for kindness.
The righteous are a group watched over by the LORD, who hears their cry; despite many afflictions, he delivers them from all troubles and protects their bones so none is broken.
will_be_killed_by evil The LORD's face is against those who do evil, to cut off their memory from the earth. Evil will kill the wicked, and those who hate the righteous will be condemned.

David's enemies seek his soul, plot his ruin, hide a net and dig a pit for him without cause, and rise as unrighteous witnesses asking about things he doesn't know. They rejoiced in his adversity, tore at him without ceasing, gnashed their teeth like profane mockers, and spoke deceitful words, crying "Aha!" David asks that they be shamed, driven like chaff by the LORD's angel, and caught in their own net.

has_fate fallen and unable to rise [workers of iniquity] The wicked are called workers of iniquity, and David asks that their hand not drive him away. At the end of the unit they are described as fallen, thrust down, and unable to rise.

l: wicked man (the wicked person described in verses 1-4), Psalms
s: He has no fear of God before his eyes and flatters himself too much to detect and hate his sin. His mouth speaks iniquity and deceit, and he has ceased to be wise and to do good. He plots iniquity on his bed, sets himself in a way that is not good, and does not abhor evil.

l: children of men (those who take refuge in God), Psalms
s: The children of men take refuge under the shadow of the LORD's wings. They will be abundantly satisfied with the abundance of his house and made to drink of the river of his pleasures.

l: loving kindness (the LORD's loving kindness), Psalms
s: The LORD's loving kindness is said to be in the heavens and is called precious. It provides the refuge under his wings that the children of men seek. David asks that it continue toward those who know the LORD.

Evildoers, also called the wicked, are enemies of the LORD who habitually plot against the righteous, borrow without repaying, and draw sword and bow against the poor and needy. The records urge not envying them: their weapons will turn on themselves, they wither like grass, and their future is cut off and destroyed.

The righteous are told to trust the LORD, do good, wait patiently, cease from anger, and depart from evil. The LORD makes their righteousness shine like light, upholds them, and keeps them from falling, and they are satisfied in famine. They give generously, speak wisdom and justice, and keep God's law in their hearts. David has never seen them forsaken, and their salvation and refuge are in the LORD, who rescues them from the wicked.

is_inherited_by righteous [also the humble who wait for the LORD] The land is the inheritance promised repeatedly to those who wait for the LORD: the humble, the blessed, and the righteous. They will dwell in it, enjoy safe pasture, and live in it forever. Those cursed by the LORD and the wicked are cut off from it.
The speaker's sin and iniquity weigh as an overwhelming burden causing bodily weakness and wounds through foolishness; he ends by resolving to confess his iniquity and be sorry for his sin.

The speaker's physical suffering, attributed to foolishness and God's indignation, begins with unsound flesh and bones, then reveals loathsome wounds, burning waist, bruising and faintness, ending in failing strength, lost eyesight, daily mourning and constant pain.

David's enemies are numerous, vigorous adversaries who hate him without cause and repay good with evil. They seek his life, lay snares, and speak deceits all day, while he fears they will gloat when his foot slips.

Humanity is portrayed as fleeting: like a breath and a walking shadow, busying itself in vain and heaping up wealth for unknown heirs. Rebuked by the LORD for iniquity, its wealth is consumed like a moth; every man is but breath.

l: human frailty and brevity of life, Psalms
s: is_a theme of the psalm [days as hand widths, a breath] David asks to know how frail he is and says the LORD has made his days handbreadths, his lifetime as nothing before the LORD. Life is likened to a breath and a shadow, and the psalm ends with the prospect of going away and existing no more. This frailty is the basis of David's plea for mercy and recovery of strength.

The psalmist is a speaker who waited patiently for the LORD and was rescued from a miry pit, given a firm place on a rock and a new song of praise. He delights in God's law, which is within his heart, and openly proclaims God's righteousness, faithfulness and salvation in the great assembly. Yet, beset by countless iniquities and evils and opposed by enemies, he calls himself poor and needy and pleads for the LORD, his helper and deliverer.

l: enemies (those who seek the psalmist's soul), Psalms
s: They seek the speaker's soul to destroy it, delight in his hurt, and say "Aha! Aha!" to him. The speaker asks that they be disappointed, confounded, turned backward, brought to dishonor, and made desolate by reason of their shame.

l: LORD's righteousness, faithfulness and salvation, Psalms
s: The speaker says he has proclaimed the LORD's righteousness as glad news in the great assembly and has not hidden it in his heart. He has also declared the LORD's faithfulness and salvation, and those who love the LORD's salvation are to say continually, "Let the LORD be exalted!"

l: he who considers the poor, Psalms
s: A person who considers the poor is declared blessed; the LORD promises to deliver, preserve, and keep him alive, not surrender him to enemies, and sustain and restore him on his sickbed.

David's enemies, called strangers, are a hostile, violent group who hate him and seek his soul without setting God before them. First they wish his death, visit with falsehood, whisper, and imagine the worst, believing his illness means he will rise no more. Later they rise up against him; David asks God to repay and destroy them, having seen triumph over them.
David's trusted familiar friend, who shared his bread, betrays him by lifting his heel against him; David lists this betrayal among troubles brought before the LORD.

afflicts David [called an evil disease by enemies] David's illness keeps him on a sickbed, and his enemies call it an evil disease from which he will not rise again. David asks the LORD to heal him and raise him up, and the psalm says the LORD will sustain and restore the one who considers the poor from his bed of illness.

The psalmist, a son of Korah, longs and thirsts for the living God like a panting deer, weeps day and night, and remembers joyfully leading crowds to God's house in festival. Now despairing, overwhelmed by waves and feeling forgotten, he calls God his rock, and repeatedly exhorts his disturbed soul to hope and praise.
The psalmist's adversaries are a hostile group who continually taunt him with "Where is your God?", wound him with reproach like a sword in his bones, and oppress him, leaving him mourning.
is_driven_back_at Exodus from Egypt The Jordan was driven back, or turned back. It is then asked why it turned back.

l: despair and hope in God, Psalms
s: The psalmist's soul is in despair and disturbed within him, and he confronts it with the same refrain twice: "Why are you in despair, my soul?" He answers it by commanding hope in God, declaring that he will still praise him as the saving help of his countenance and his God.

is ungodly The ungodly nation is the party against whom the speaker asks God to plead his cause. It is mentioned alongside deceitful and wicked men from whom he seeks deliverance, and the enemy's oppression is the cause of his mourning.

The people, speaking as 'we' and 'I', recall that their fathers won the land through God and not their own sword, and they declare they will not trust in their bow. Now they are rejected, scattered among the nations, plundered, and mocked, yet they insist they have not forgotten God, been false to his covenant, or turned from his path. They are killed all day long, regarded as sheep for slaughter, and bowed down to the dust as they plead for help and redemption.

In the past, the nations and peoples were driven out and afflicted by God so that his people could be planted in the land, and the speakers say God shamed those who hated them. In the present, those who hate the people take plunder, cause them to turn back, and taunt, reproach, and verbally abuse them. The enemy and the avenger are the cause of the speaker's shame.

A communal lament over national defeat and suffering: the people retreat before the adversary, are plundered, scattered, sold cheaply, mocked, crushed and killed, covered in shame. They insist they stayed faithful, and blame God's rejection and hidden face for the reversal.

The king is praised as the most excellent of the sons of men, with grace on his lips and blessed by God forever. His throne endures forever and ever, ruled by an equitable scepter. God anointed him with the oil of gladness above his fellows because he loves righteousness and hates wickedness. He is fragrant with myrrh, aloes, and cassia, dwells in ivory palaces, and is attended by honorable women, with the queen at his right hand. He rides victoriously against enemies, and his sons will become princes in all the earth.

The queen is a royal figure clothed in gold of Ophir, interwoven with gold, standing at the king's right hand among honorable women. She is urged to listen, forget her people and father's house, and honor the king, who will desire her beauty; virgin companions follow.

A wedding psalm, labeled a contemplation by the sons of Korah for the Chief Musician, set to "The Lilies." The speaker addresses the king in praise, describes the queen and the princess's glorious procession with companions into the palace, and promises the king's name will be remembered and thanked forever.

Mount Zion is the holy city of God, the place of the Most High's tents, beautiful in elevation and the joy of the whole earth. Most important is its immovable stability, since God dwells within it, loves it, and will establish it forever. It is gladdened by a river's streams, and its towers, bulwarks, palaces and citadels show God as refuge. The records move from God's help and presence in the city, to its beauty and fortifications, to God's choice of it and Judah and the building of his sanctuary, and finally to its image as unmovable, to which those who trust the LORD are compared.
The nations raged and the kingdoms were moved, but God lifted his voice and the earth melted. God declares that he will be exalted among them, and he ends wars to the end of the earth.

The earth is described as changing, with mountains shaken into the heart of the seas, and as melting when God lifts his voice. It is the place where God has made desolations, ends wars, and declares he will be exalted.
